items.followUp: What is a Denial of Service attack?

rubric.description: Gives the full form of DoS.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct expansion.

rubric.why: Explains the effect of a DoS attack.
rubric.description: States that the attack makes a computer or service unavailable to users.

modelAnswer: DoS stands for Denial of Service.
It is an attack that makes a computer or network service unavailable to its users.

items.followUp: How can attackers use a vulnerability scanner?

rubric.why: Explains that scanning is used to find website weaknesses.
rubric.description: States that attackers scan websites for vulnerabilities or weaknesses.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying this purpose.

rubric.why: Explains how the discovered weaknesses can be misused.
rubric.description: States that attackers may exploit the weaknesses to attack or gain access to the website.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining the resulting misuse.

modelAnswer: Cybercriminals scan websites to find security weaknesses or vulnerabilities.
They may exploit these weaknesses to attack the website or gain unauthorized access.

items.followUp: What is written in the body section of an HTML document?

rubric.description: States that the head is a section of an HTML document.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as the document's head section.

rubric.why: Describes the kind of information held in the head.
rubric.description: States that it contains document information such as the title or metadata, which is generally not displayed on the page.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct description of its contents or display.

modelAnswer: The head section is the part of an HTML document enclosed by the <head> and </head> tags.
It contains information about the document, such as its title, which is generally not displayed in the webpage.
